question_stem:
A hot-air balloon floats just above the ground. The balloon is stationary and is held in place by a vertical rope, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

{{figure:figure_2_1}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.part_stem: The balloon has a weight $W$ of $3.39 \times 10^4 \text{N}$. The tension $T$ in the rope is $4.00 \times 10^2 \text{N}$. Upthrust $U$ acts on the balloon. The density of the surrounding air is $1.23 \text{kg m}^{-3}$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: On Fig. 2.1, draw labelled arrows to show the directions of the three forces acting on the balloon.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the volume, to three significant figures, of the balloon.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
The balloon is released from the rope.

Calculate the initial acceleration of the balloon.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The balloon is stationary at a height of $500 \text{m}$ above the ground. A tennis ball is released from rest and falls vertically from the balloon.

A passenger in the balloon uses the equation $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ to calculate that the ball will be travelling at a speed of approximately $100 \text{m s}^{-1}$ when it hits the ground.

Explain why the actual speed of the ball will be much lower than $100 \text{m s}^{-1}$ when it hits the ground.

parts.label: (c)
parts.part_stem: Before the balloon is released, the rope holding the balloon has a strain of $2.4 \times 10^{-5}$. The rope has an unstretched length of $2.5 \text{m}$. The rope obeys Hooke's law.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Show that the extension of the rope is $6.0 \times 10^{-5} \text{m}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the elastic potential energy $E_{\text{P}}$ of the rope.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The rope holding the balloon is replaced with a new one of the same original length and cross-sectional area. The tension is unchanged and the new rope also obeys Hooke's law.

The new rope is made from a material of a lower Young modulus.

State and explain the effect of the lower Young modulus on the elastic potential energy of the rope.
